title: Restriction of a counit-defined structural coefficient mate
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{\times}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}\to R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K\to F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Assume the named dualizing objects are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Define $u_Y:T_Y\omega_{Y,A}\to\omega_{Y,B}$ to be the unique map with $\varepsilon_{Y,B}F_{Y,B}(u_Y)=(T_s\varepsilon_{Y,A})c_{Y,\omega_{Y,A}}^{-1}$, using $T_sA_s\cong B_s$. For an affine open $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$, identify $j^*\omega_{Y,R}\cong\omega_{U,R}$ using the counit-compatible open structural adjunction, and identify $j^*T_Y\cong T_Uj^*$ by the canonical tensor/pullback comparison [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Then
$$j^*u_Y=u_U.$$
More explicitly put $W=\omega_{Y,A}$, $L=j^*W$, let $e_R:j_{!,R}j^*\to1$ be evaluation and $d_L:T_Yj_{!,A}L\cong j_{!,B}T_UL$ the canonical open tensor isomorphism [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. With the canonical compact-support compositions understood, the equality of adjuncts is
$$\varepsilon_{U,B}F_{U,B}(j^*u_Y)=(T_s\varepsilon_{Y,A})c_{Y,W}^{-1}F_{Y,B}(T_Ye_{A,W})F_{Y,B}(d_L)^{-1}=(T_s\varepsilon_{U,A})c_{U,L}^{-1}.$$
All inverse coefficient components here are at bounded constructible finite-Tor objects $W,j_{!,A}L,L$; the assertion does not assume a coefficient comparison for an exceptional adjoint.

The proper scalar comparison is invertible on all inputs by [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension]: the base is a Noetherian field spectrum and c.Z is Noetherian by finite type and quasi-compactness. proof.text: Identify ExceptionalCoefficients.openIso with openScalarExtension using the proved open-unit comparison compactScalarOpen_eq in [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence]. Apply the counit clause of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor] at W. Cancel the open comparison, apply naturality of B-open evaluation at globalMate, and then its defining Hom-transpose equation. Apply global B-compact support and compose the structural counit. This gives restrictedMate_adjunct, the second conjunct of Formula, with middleAdjunct exactly as defined.

proof.text: Apply ordinary-etale scalar/open composition [lem-pur-etale-open-scalar-composition] to j followed by c.i. Naturality of scalarMate for the same proper map c.g, evaluated at the inverse open compositor, gives compactSupportMap_open_composition. Cancel its invertible coefficient components to obtain localInverse_eq. The naturality equation compactScalarMap_naturality of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], after cancellation of coefficient maps, gives inverse_naturality. Apply it to A-open evaluation, then expand the composite adjunction counit. This is middleAdjunct_eq, the third conjunct of Formula.
